options.content:
### New York City 311 service requests

311 is New York's number for everything that is not an emergency: a car across a driveway, a party
next door, no heat, a pothole, a dead tree. Each call, app report or web form becomes a *service
request*, passed to the agency that handles it, and published on NYC Open Data with where it was,
what it was about and when it was closed.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Source** | [311 Service Requests from 2010 to Present](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Social-Services/311-Service-Requests-from-2010-to-Present/erm2-nwe9) (NYC Open Data, Socrata), read through the gateway's `/nyc311/` route |
| **Window** | the last four weeks (28 days, so each day of the week counts four times), from midnight New York time; Open Data publishes requests a few days after they are made, so the last days are empty or partial |
| **Pipeline** | the server's DuckDB reads one CSV, which the gateway builds from Socrata at most once an hour → Chaski, DuckDB in your browser → every panel, with Mosaic for the linked views |
| **Licence** | NYC Open Data [terms of use](https://www.nyc.gov/home/terms-of-use.page): free to use |

**Themes** group the 173 complaint types by the agency that answers them: NYPD's parking and vehicle
complaints, every *Noise* type (NYPD and DEP), HPD's housing conditions (heat, plumbing, paint,
leaks), DSNY's sanitation, DOT's streets, signs and street lights, DEP, Parks and Health together as
*Environment* (water, sewers, trees, rodents), NYPD's other matters with Homeless Services as *Street
life*, and Buildings with the rest as *Other*.
**Closed** is how long a request took, from when it was made to when the agency closed it; a request
closed is not always a problem fixed (NYPD closes a noise call once officers have answered it).
Under 2 % of requests have no place and are left off the map, not off the counts.

**Everything is answered in your browser.** The timeline, the filters, the map and the charts share
one Mosaic selection: pick themes or boroughs, brush the hours, press play or draw an area on the map,
and the rest follows. Times are New York's on the timeline and in the week chart.

-- All four weeks, once: the filters reach the map as Mosaic clauses and are applied
-- there, on the GPU, with no query.

FROM $requests
WHERE latitude IS NOT NULL

spec.description: Requests made in each 12 hours of the four weeks. Drag to keep a window, press play to slide it.
spec.title: Timeline

spec.rawSql:
SELECT type AS "Complaint", theme AS "Theme",
       count(*)::DOUBLE AS "Requests",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE closed_in = 'Still open')::DOUBLE AS "Still open",
       round(median(hours), 1) AS "Median hours",
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE hours <= 24) / nullif(count(hours), 0)) AS "In a day (%)"
FROM $requests
WHERE $__crossfilter($requestFilters)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY "Requests" DESC
LIMIT 50

spec.description: Four weeks of 311 requests in the browser, read by the server through the gateway when the dashboard opens.
spec.name: requests

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per visit: New York City's 311 service requests of the last four weeks
-- (NYC Open Data, dataset erm2-nwe9), through the gateway (http://feeds/nyc311/...), which
-- builds /nyc311/requests/<day>.csv from Socrata (it takes Socrata two minutes) and keeps
-- one copy for every visitor. The URL names the day 28 days ago; past midnight the gateway
-- may still hand over yesterday's copy while it builds today's, so the window is cut here.
-- Socrata keeps New York wall-clock time with no zone: time is UTC here, the clock of the
-- map and the timeline; hour and day stay New York's, for the week chart.
SET force_download = true;
-- The setting would outlive this query on the pooled connection it ran on, and stop the range reads of every Parquet read there later, so the result goes through a temp table (one per connection) and the setting is put back before it is returned.
SET VARIABLE since = (timezone('America/New_York', now())::DATE - 28)::TIMESTAMP;
SET VARIABLE url = 'http://feeds/nyc311/requests/' || strftime(getvariable('since'), '%Y-%m-%d') || '.csv';
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE fd_nyc311_1 AS
WITH r AS (
  SELECT * FROM read_csv(getvariable('url'), header = true,
    -- Socrata writes a quote inside a field doubled (""No Smoking""), the CSV standard;
    -- DuckDB's sniffer sometimes guesses no escape at all and fails the whole read.
    quote = '"', escape = '"', columns = {
    'unique_key': 'BIGINT', 'created_date': 'TIMESTAMP', 'closed_date': 'TIMESTAMP',
    'agency': 'VARCHAR', 'complaint_type': 'VARCHAR', 'descriptor': 'VARCHAR',
    'status': 'VARCHAR', 'borough': 'VARCHAR', 'latitude': 'DOUBLE', 'longitude': 'DOUBLE',
    'open_data_channel_type': 'VARCHAR'})
)
SELECT
  unique_key::VARCHAR AS id,
  timezone('UTC', timezone('America/New_York', created_date)) AS time,
  -- Eight themes from 173 complaint types, by the agency that answers them: the map's
  -- and the charts' colours.
  CASE WHEN complaint_type ILIKE 'noise%' THEN 'Noise'
       WHEN agency = 'HPD' THEN 'Housing'
       WHEN agency = 'NYPD' AND regexp_matches(complaint_type, '(?i)parking|vehicle|driveway') THEN 'Parking'
       WHEN agency IN ('NYPD', 'DHS') THEN 'Street life'
       WHEN agency = 'DSNY' THEN 'Sanitation'
       WHEN agency = 'DOT' THEN 'Streets'
       WHEN agency IN ('DEP', 'DPR', 'DOHMH') THEN 'Environment'
       ELSE 'Other' END AS theme,
  complaint_type AS type,
  descriptor,
  agency,
  CASE borough WHEN 'MANHATTAN' THEN 'Manhattan' WHEN 'BROOKLYN' THEN 'Brooklyn'
               WHEN 'QUEENS' THEN 'Queens' WHEN 'BRONX' THEN 'The Bronx'
               WHEN 'STATEN ISLAND' THEN 'Staten Island' ELSE 'Unspecified' END AS borough,
  CASE open_data_channel_type WHEN 'ONLINE' THEN 'Online' WHEN 'MOBILE' THEN 'App'
                              WHEN 'PHONE' THEN 'Phone' ELSE 'Unknown' END AS channel,
  -- Hours from the request to its closing: none while it is open, nor for the few
  -- hundred closed before they were made.
  CASE WHEN status = 'Closed' AND closed_date >= created_date
       THEN round(epoch(closed_date - created_date) / 3600, 2) END AS hours,
  CASE WHEN status IS DISTINCT FROM 'Closed' THEN 'Still open'
       WHEN closed_date IS NULL OR closed_date < created_date THEN 'Time unknown'
       WHEN closed_date - created_date < INTERVAL 1 HOUR THEN 'Within an hour'
       WHEN closed_date - created_date < INTERVAL 1 DAY THEN 'Within a day'
       WHEN closed_date - created_date < INTERVAL 7 DAY THEN 'Within a week'
       ELSE 'After a week' END AS closed_in,
  hour(created_date) AS hour,
  strftime(created_date, '%a') AS day,
  round(latitude, 5) AS latitude,
  round(longitude, 5) AS longitude
FROM r
WHERE created_date >= getvariable('since')
ORDER BY time
;
SET force_download = false;
SELECT * FROM fd_nyc311_1
